X.note: The bastion wall has a decent limestone texture, but the parapet is missing and the gun deck is a flat, blotchy gravel slab, so the top reads like a cut-off platform. The wall is pale and clean with no weathering. The background buildings are untextured grey boxes. The frames look stable.

Y.note: The wall is a smooth, pale, near-featureless extrusion with only faint fine noise. The deck is a dark asphalt-like slab that looks like a modern tarmac roof. It reads as a clay or white-card model, with a modern feel and no weathering. The frames are stable.

Z.note: The bastion has a coursed ashlar wall with a stone parapet, a string course, waterline algae staining and weathering. The earthen terreplein with guns reads as a plausible 18th-century gun platform. The texture stays locked to the wall across the frames. The weak spots are the untextured grey block buildings behind it and the slightly uniform staining.

why: Z has the convincing weathered coursed masonry, a parapet and an earthen gun terrace, while Y is a smooth, toy-like white shape with an asphalt-looking deck and X sits in between with a missing parapet and a pale clean wall.
anachronisms_seen: asphalt/tarmac-like dark deck surface (Y, partly X)
no parapet on the gun platform (X, Y)
untextured modern-looking flat-roofed grey block buildings in the background (all)
